query: What product attributes are associated with higher satisfaction scores?

per_column.name: taste_quality
per_column.rationale: A clear ordinal taste axis to correlate with Score; useful for the query. Values track source text well (excellent for the confection, poor for medicinal cherry soda). Overlaps somewhat with product_quality_assessment but is a distinct sensory dimension.

per_column.name: product_quality_assessment
per_column.rationale: Overall quality grade is relevant, but largely redundant with taste_quality (near-identical values across samples), reducing added leverage. Values are well-grounded in the text.

per_column.name: freshness_delivery_condition
per_column.rationale: Delivery/freshness is a genuine separate attribute and appropriately NULL when unmentioned (~39% null is fine). However, assigning 'fresh_good_condition' to the confection and 'acceptable' to the mislabeled-peanuts and cough-medicine rows where condition is not discussed is an unwarranted specific rather than NULL, weakening groundedness.

per_column.name: ingredient_quality_naturalness
per_column.rationale: Ingredient/naturalness is a plausible new axis. But several values overreach: the mislabeled peanuts (a labeling complaint) marked 'quality_positive', and the powdered-sugar confection also 'quality_positive' though naturalness is not addressed. Some values assert positives not supported by text.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Price/value is a distinct and useful attribute (taffy explicitly praises price). However, many rows lack any price mention yet receive confident values (dog food 'good_value', confection 'good_value', cough soda 'fair_value'), which are invented specifics where NULL was warranted.

per_column.name: product_consistency_reliability
per_column.rationale: Consistency across batches is a valid axis, but most single-review texts give no basis for a consistency judgment; defaulting to 'mostly_consistent' for the confection, taffy, and cough soda is unsupported inference. Groundedness is weak.

per_column.name: competitive_product_standing
per_column.rationale: Competitive positioning would be useful if grounded, but most reviews make no competitor comparison; assigning 'comparable_to_competitors' by default to the confection, cough soda, and taffy asserts information absent from the text. Frequently ungrounded specifics.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: A binary repurchase-intent signal is a reasonable modeling axis and correlates plausibly with satisfaction. Values are defensible sentiment reads (recommend->True, complaints->False), though inferred rather than explicit in some rows.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively offer several genuine attribute axes (taste, value, freshness, repurchase intent) directly relevant to relating product attributes to satisfaction, with only mild redundancy between taste_quality and product_quality_assessment. Groundedness is the weaker dimension: freshness, value, consistency, and especially competitive_standing frequently emit confident specific values for rows whose text is silent on those aspects, where NULL would have been correct, indicating a tendency to assert unsupported specifics rather than abstain.
